subject: Hosted API: p95/p99 spike — upstream TLS/CDN delays / BlueBay Logistics escalation
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@bluebaylogistics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in API latency — p99 up to 2.1s (samples attached)

Alex —

We started seeing a regression in Hosted API latency this morning around 08:45 PDT. p95/p99 for first-token response jumped from ~280ms to ~1.8–2.1s, and our dashboards show a corresponding surge in error rate for short requests (single-shot prompt flows). We captured a couple of cURL timings and a short tcpdump during a failing window — attaching the traces.

Key notes:
- Sample request: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- curl --write-out "%{time_starttransfer}\n" shows ~1.88s
- tcpdump shows TLS handshake timeouts and prolonged ClientHello->ServerHello delays (mostly in us-east-1 edge IP blocks)
- No changes from our side; this coincides with our morning traffic increase but magnitude is outside normal variance

Please escalate — this is impacting production customers and our SLAs. We need an estimate for a mitigation plan and expected ETA for fix or a recommended temporary workaround.

Attachments: bluebay_request_trace.txt (curl & tcpdump snippets)

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Ops Lead, BlueBay Logistics
lydia@bluebaylogistics.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, lydia@bluebaylogistics.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in API latency — p99 up to 2.1s (samples attached)

Forwarding BlueBay's traces — they report first-token spikes and TCP/TLS timing anomalies focused at us-east edges. Can ops take a look and confirm whether this is an upstream CDN/edge issue or something in our connection handling?

Customer impact: production routes, p99 ~2s for many short calls, increased errors. They want an ETA and temporary workaround. Please prioritize — looping in Laura given SLA exposure.

Attachments forwarded: bluebay_request_trace.txt

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: nora@fastedgecdn.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in API latency — initial triage (grabbed pcap + short-term mitigation)

Thanks for the heads up and traces — I pulled the customer's samples and matched them against our edge telemetry. Initial findings:

- The curl traces line up with a long TLS handshake phase (time to first byte inflated, TCP connect is normal). The majority of the delay is in TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (server-side processing / upstream edge routing).
- Our logs show a cluster of increased handshake durations originating from a small set of us-east edge IPs (likely FastEdge POPs) between 08:42–09:10 PDT.
- Error spike correlates with handshake timeouts and occasional 5xx when we hit our per-connection timeout thresholds.

Attachments: latency-sample.csv (aggregated p95/p99 by POP), diagnostic_pcap.zip (sanitized pcap of Customer session)

Immediate mitigations to reduce customer pain:
1) Policy-based routing: move BlueBay traffic to alternate POPs/regions where handshake times are normal (risk: slight egress latency increase but reduces TTFT).
2) Enable connection reuse / keep-alive hints on the front-door for their client IP block (low-risk, immediate drop in handshake frequency).
3) Ask FastEdge (nora@fastedgecdn.com) to confirm abnormal CPU / TLS handshake queues on the implicated nodes; request accelerated remediation.

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- 10:20 PDT: Execute targeted traffic shift for BlueBay to alternate edge.
- 10:30 PDT: Monitor p95/p99 and confirm reduction.
- 11:00 PDT: If stable, coordinate with BlueBay CS for longer-term config and credits.

I'll run the routing change now and report back. Alex/Marissa — please advise if BlueBay needs a specific maintenance window before we move traffic.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Infrastructure Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@bluebaylogistics.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in API latency — customer update and proposed mitigation

Hi Lydia —

Thanks for the traces and patience. Sean has identified the likely cause as intermittent TLS handshake queuing at a subset of our us-east CDN edges. We're planning a targeted traffic shift for your account to alternate POPs in ~5 minutes, which should lower your first-token latencies. Expected customer-facing impact: brief (sub-second) re-routing with no request loss.

We also propose a one-time courtesy credit for the affected window. Can you confirm we may proceed with the immediate traffic shift? If you prefer a scheduled window we can coordinate a specific minute, but our preference is immediate to minimize ongoing errors.

We will follow up with a fuller RCA and a timeline for permanent fix (we are engaging the CDN vendor).

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll keep you posted every 15 minutes while we monitor.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:35:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary / next steps for BlueBay outage window

Team — thanks for the rapid response. Two asks for exec/CS-facing comms:

1) Prepare a one-paragraph customer-facing summary (what happened, what we did, next steps + ETA for RCA) and a short internal timeline of events (for legal/compliance). Target: 30 minutes.
2) Please draft leniency/credit calculation and proposed messaging for account owner (Alex) to approve. We should also notify revenue ops for possible SLA adjustment on the deal.

Sean — I want a concise root-cause hypothesis and the extent of impact across accounts (how many customers/regions affected). If this is isolated to FastEdge nodes, we need the vendor's incident id and remediation ETA.

I'll join a quick triage call if helpful — ping calendar and include infra lead.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference
